subject: Clarify reserved pool throughput & queueing behavior — PhotonPay request
messages:
From: Ben Turner <ben.turner@photonpay.com>

Cc: Sarah Li <s.li@photonpay.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool throughput during launch spike

Markus —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We have a tight launch window for a payments feature and expect a sustained 10x spike in inference calls for ~48 hours, with short bursts above that. Our procurement cycle is still finalizing the reserved capacity contract, but we need operational assurances to prevent queueing/backpressure from impacting production during the launch.

Questions:
- Can Redwood guarantee a minimum sustained throughput (tokens/sec or rps) on a reserved pool while procurement finishes?
- How will the platform behave if our reserved pool is saturated? Specifically: will requests queue indefinitely, fail fast, or auto-burst to other pools/regions?
- What controls can we set (queue size, max latency threshold, fallback model)? We need to map SLOs to expected errors and retries.

I've attached our short load test (CSV) and a suggested SLA language from our legal team. Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can make a go/no-go decision.

Ben

Ben —

Thanks for sending the numbers and the draft SLA language. Short answer: we can support this, but we need to be explicit about what "guarantee" means during the procurement gap.

Quick summary of behavior and options from the platform side:
- Reserved pool baseline: when you reserve GPUs we can configure a baseline throughput target expressed in concurrent tokens/sec for the pool. That baseline can be honored while procurement completes if you opt into a short-term credit/commitment arrangement.
- Burst policy: by default the pool will try to burst to capacity in the same region (other compatible dedicated pools) up to a configured cap. If bursting is exhausted, requests enter an internal queue that applies backpressure and uses priority scoring (prefix cache hits and customer SLA tier). Queue length is bounded and requests beyond that are rejected with 429.
- Latency SLOs: we target p50/p95/p99 latencies for token-generation under normal load; during saturated bursts p99 can jump — we can configure an emergency fallback to a smaller, lower-cost model with graceful degradation rather than queueing.

What we need from PhotonPay to proceed quickly:
1) Confirmation you accept a temporary credit-backed reservation that covers the 48hr window (our finance team needs a short PO or card auth).
2) A prioritized list of endpoints/prompts to protect (so we can route only critical traffic through the reserved pool).
3) If you want the fallback-to-smaller-model option, tell us which quality drop is acceptable (e.g., 5–10% latency reduction vs. expected accuracy).

I'm looping in Vivek (infra SLA owner) to propose a concrete operational playbook and a short SLA addendum you can sign this week.

—Priyom
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool throughput during launch spike

Ben —

Appreciate the urgency. Below is a proposed operational playbook we can implement immediately once we have a short-term finance authorization. I also attached a revised SLA snippet with explicit queueing behavior.

Operational playbook (short term, 72 hours):
- Reserve: allocate a temporary reserved pool equivalent to 12 reserved vGPUs (matches your peak RPS from the CSV).
- Baseline throughput: configure pool baseline at 85% capacity to leave headroom for autoscaling decisions at the node level.
- Burst policy: enable intra-region burst to compatible dedicated pools up to +25% of baseline. Additional bursts will not be permitted without an explicit emergency escalation to our on-call.
- Queueing: bounded FIFO queue per-customer with a 60s time-to-live. If a request sits >60s it returns 429 with the header X-Redwood-Queue-Time and our recommended retry-after of 30s. We will also surface telemetry and alerts to your SRE channel.
- Fallback model: automatic fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant (lower compute) after queue occupancy >70% for more than 2 minutes. That fallback is opt-in and degrades semantic fidelity slightly.

Risk/notes:
- We cannot provide an unconditional unlimited-burst guarantee without an executed reserved contract. The short-term credit auth is the operational mechanism to ensure we can prioritize capacity behind the scenes.
- If you require contractual uptime/latency credits tied to this temporary window we can draft a one-off addendum but will need legal and finance sign-off (48–72 hours).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Ben, confirm authorization method (card auth or short PO) today so we can allocate the pool tomorrow morning.
2) Provide the list of endpoints to protect and the acceptable degradation profile for fallback.
3) Mark (cc'd) to approve the addendum language for legal review.

I'll attach the SLA snippet now.

—Vivek

Ben —

Thanks for the patience. PhotonPay is an existing strategic pipeline account and we want to avoid any outage during your launch. I approve the short-term reservation plan described below subject to Finance taking the card authorization. Summary of what Redwood will do once we receive authorization:
- Allocate 12 reserved vGPUs in us-west-2 for 72 hours, baseline at 85% capacity with +25% regional burst enabled as described.
- Enforce bounded queue with 60s TTL and 429 responses thereafter; X-Redwood-Queue-Time will be included for observability.
- Enable opt-in fallback to the 8-bit quantized model after sustained queue occupancy.
- Our SRE will open a dedicated Slack channel and provide live telemetry for the window.

We will not be able to extend unlimited auto-burst beyond the +25% cap without a signed reserved contract. If you need contractual credits for SLA misses during the window, our Legal/Finance teams must sign the addendum (we can fast-track this if you push an executive sign-off).

If you confirm card auth now and send the list of critical endpoints, we will target allocation by 06:00 PT tomorrow.
